subproblem.title: Zero current, mass of integer combinations, finite integer combinations of IM currents
subproblem.statement: (a) For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every U ⊆ ℝ^P, the zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity. (b) For all P, n, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, currents A, B, C ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and integers p, q with A(ω) = p·B(ω) + q·C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), one has M_W(A) ≤ |p|·M_W(B) + |q|·M_W(C) in [0, ∞] for every W ⊆ ℝ^P. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (Euclidean coefficient norm), and M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X). (c) Assume (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the difference A − B is integer multiplicity. Then for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every type ι, finite set F ⊆ ι, currents S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (i ∈ ι) that are integer multiplicity for i ∈ F, and integers m_i (i ∈ ι), there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = Σ_{i∈F} m_i·S_i(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and M_W(Y) ≤ Σ_{i∈F} |m_i|·M_W(S_i) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 0(ii) (the zero current is IM via the empty IMRep; with (IMC)(c), A + B := A − (0 − B) and all integer combinations of IM currents are IM) and step 0(iii) (masses are subadditive); Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756: p₁T₁ + p₂T₂ is integer multiplicity) and 2.4–2.5 (definition of M_W). Call ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) W-admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W); then M_W(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over W-admissible ω.
1. (a) Let R be the IMRep in U with carrier ∅, multiplicity ≡ 0 and orientation ≡ 0. Its fields hold: ∅ is measurable and ∅ ⊆ U; ∅ is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, since μHE[n] ∅ = 0); a constant multiplicity is measurable and positivity on ∅ is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅∩K} θ dHⁿ = 0 ≠ ∞; a constant orientation is a.e. strongly measurable; and μHE[n].restrict ∅ = 0, so the a.e. orientation condition holds trivially. For every ω, R.action(ω) = ∫_∅ … dHⁿ = 0 = 0(ω). So R represents 0 and 0 is integer multiplicity.
2. A symmetric bound. Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and let ω be W-admissible. Then −ω is W-admissible, because tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω (tsupport_neg) and |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). Since X(−ω) = −X(ω) (linearity), ofReal|X(ω)| equals ofReal(X(ω)) or ofReal(X(−ω)), and both are ≤ M_W(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Hence ofReal|X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X).
3. (b) Let ω be W-admissible. Then A(ω) = pB(ω) + qC(ω) ≤ |p||B(ω)| + |q||C(ω)|. By monotonicity of ofReal, ofReal_add (both summands are ≥ 0) and ofReal_mul, ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ ofReal|p|·ofReal|B(ω)| + ofReal|q|·ofReal|C(ω)| ≤ |p|·M_W(B) + |q|·M_W(C), using step 2 and ofReal|p| = (p.natAbs : [0, ∞]) (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast, Nat.cast_natAbs, Int.cast_abs). Taking the supremum over ω (sSup_le) proves (b). In particular, with A = B = C = 0 and p = q = 0, M_W(0) = 0.
4. (c), integer multiples. Assume (IMC)(c), let U be open and X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity. By induction on k ∈ ℕ there is an integer multiplicity V_k with V_k(ω) = k·X(ω) for all ω and M_W(V_k) ≤ k·M_W(X) for all W: V_0 := 0 (integer multiplicity by (a), M_W(0) = 0 by step 3); V_{k+1} := V_k − (0 − X), which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) applied to 0 and X and then to V_k and 0 − X, has values V_k(ω) − (0 − X(ω)) = (k+1)X(ω), and, since V_{k+1}(ω) = 1·V_k(ω) + 1·X(ω), satisfies M_W(V_{k+1}) ≤ M_W(V_k) + M_W(X) ≤ (k+1)M_W(X) by (b). For m ∈ ℤ: if m = |m| take V := V_{|m|}; if m = −|m| take V := 0 − V_{|m|}, which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c), has V(ω) = −|m|X(ω) = mX(ω) and, by (b) with (p, q) = (−1, 0), M_W(V) ≤ M_W(V_{|m|}) ≤ |m|M_W(X). So for every m ∈ ℤ there is an integer multiplicity V with V(ω) = m·X(ω) and M_W(V) ≤ |m|·M_W(X) for all ω, W.
5. (c), induction on the finite set F (Finset.induction_on). If F = ∅, Y := 0 works: it is integer multiplicity by (a), Y(ω) = 0 is the empty sum, and M_W(Y) = 0 by step 3. If F' = F ∪ {j} with j ∉ F and S_i integer multiplicity for i ∈ F', the induction hypothesis gives Y_F for F, and step 4 gives an integer multiplicity V with V(ω) = m_jS_j(ω) and M_W(V) ≤ |m_j|M_W(S_j). Put Y := Y_F − (0 − V): it is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) twice; Y(ω) = Y_F(ω) + V(ω) = Σ_{i∈F} m_iS_i(ω) + m_jS_j(ω) = Σ_{i∈F'} m_iS_i(ω) (Finset.sum_insert); and by (b) with p = q = 1, M_W(Y) ≤ M_W(Y_F) + M_W(V) ≤ Σ_{i∈F}|m_i|M_W(S_i) + |m_j|M_W(S_j) = Σ_{i∈F'}|m_i|M_W(S_i). ∎
proof_key_steps: The IMRep with empty carrier represents the zero current.
−ω is admissible with ω, so ofReal|X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X); hence M_W(A) ≤ |p|M_W(B) + |q|M_W(C) when A = pB + qC.
Under (IMC)(c), integer multiples m·X are built by iterated differences with 0, with mass ≤ |m|M_W(X).
Finset induction gives finite integer combinations that are integer multiplicity with the summed mass bound.

Source: parent proof step 7 (V4(o)). The slice currents T⌞{f<t}, (∂T)⌞{f<t}, Y⌞{f<t}, (∂Y)⌞{f<t} of the parent's step 0(i) are obtained here from (SL), which asserts their existence. Notation: E_t := {f < t}.
1. Representations. Apply (REP) with U := ℝ^P to T, ∂T, Y and ∂Y (they have locally finite mass). This gives (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ_Y, ξ_Y), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) with measures finite on compact sets, a.e. strongly measurable fields with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x (hence a.e.), and T(ω) = ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T, ∂T(η) = ∫ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T}, Y(ω) = ∫ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y, ∂Y(η) = ∫ξ_{∂Y}(η)dμ_{∂Y}. These are admissible representations in the sense of the integer slice property.
2. Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of T − Y and ∂(T − Y), and let f be L-Lipschitz; E_t is Borel for every t because f is continuous.
3. The integer slice property of T, applied to (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), f, L, gives a null set N_T such that for t ∉ N_T every pair of currents satisfying the slice formulas for these representations has integer multiplicity ∂A − B; likewise the property of Y gives a null set N_Y. N := N_T ∪ N_Y is null.
4. (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, applied to T with (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), f, L (its hypotheses hold by step 1), gives currents A^T_t, B^T_t with A^T_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T and B^T_t(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T} for every t; likewise (SL) applied to Y gives A^Y_t, B^Y_t.
5. Linearity of restrictions. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P), ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = T(ω) = (T − Y)(ω) + Y(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ + ∫ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y. Hence (RU) (k := d + 1, U := ℝ^P, triples (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ, ξ), (μ_Y, ξ_Y), whose hypotheses hold by step 1 and admissibility) with B := E_t gives ∫_{E_t}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ + ∫_{E_t}ξ_Y(ω)dμ_Y. For every η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), ∂T(η) = T(dη) = (T − Y)(dη) + Y(dη) = ∂(T − Y)(η) + ∂Y(η), so (RU) with k := d and the triples (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ', ξ'), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) gives ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂T}(η)dμ_{∂T} = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' + ∫_{E_t}ξ_{∂Y}(η)dμ_{∂Y}.
6. Fix t ∉ N and currents A, B with A(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. By step 5, A(ω) = A^T_t(ω) − A^Y_t(ω) and B(η) = B^T_t(η) − B^Y_t(η). Hence for every η, (∂A − B)(η) = A(dη) − B(η) = [A^T_t(dη) − B^T_t(η)] − [A^Y_t(dη) − B^Y_t(η)], i.e. ∂A − B = (∂A^T_t − B^T_t) − (∂A^Y_t − B^Y_t) (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
7. By step 3, applied to the pairs (A^T_t, B^T_t) and (A^Y_t, B^Y_t), both brackets are integer multiplicity, so ∂A − B is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c). Since N is null and (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ'), f were arbitrary, T − Y has the integer slice property. ∎

(SL) provides slice currents of T and of Y for every t.
(RU) turns T = (T − Y) + Y and ∂T = ∂(T − Y) + ∂Y into the same identities for integrals over {f < t}.
Hence ∂A − B = (∂A^T_t − B^T_t) − (∂A^Y_t − B^Y_t), which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c).

Source: parent proof step 3, case n = 1 ("H⁰ is the counting measure, so θ ≥ 1 on M₀ and, by (MR), M_G(∂T) = Σ_{x∈M₀∩G}θ(x); by (VO) this vanishes for open G disjoint from spt ∂T, so M₀ ⊆ spt ∂T, and M₀ is finite (local integrability on the compact set spt ∂T). As in degree 0 the orientation is ±⟨·⟩ … so ∂T(g) = Σ m_i⟨g(x_i)⟩"), stated for an arbitrary compactly supported integer multiplicity 0-current S.
1. Let R = (M₀, θ, ζ) be an IMRep of S in ℝ^P (degree 0). H⁰ := μHE[0] equals μH[0] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), so H⁰({x}) = 1 for every x (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence H⁰(t) = #t for every finite set t (sum_measure_singleton).
2. Carrier points have positive mass: for x ∈ M₀, R.measure({x}) = ∫⁻_{{x}} θ dH⁰ = θ(x)H⁰({x}) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, lintegral_singleton, field mult_pos).
3. M₀ ⊆ spt S. Let G := ℝ^P ∖ spt S; it is the zero region of S, a union of open sets, hence open. Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G has tsupport disjoint from spt S, so S(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence M_G(S) = 0. By (MR) (U = ℝ^P, W = G open), R.measure(G) = M_G(S) = 0. If x ∈ M₀ ∩ G, then R.measure({x}) ≤ R.measure(G) = 0, contradicting step 2. So M₀ ⊆ spt S.
4. M₀ is finite. By the field locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set spt S and step 3, ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ < ∞. If M₀ were infinite, then for every N ∈ ℕ there is a finite t ⊆ M₀ with #t = N (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq), and N = H⁰(t) = ∫⁻_t 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ (θ ≥ 1 on M₀); so ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ = ∞, a contradiction. Let F be the finite set M₀.
5. The orientation is ±⟨·⟩ at every carrier point. Let B be the set of x for which no subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M₀ x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ(x)) Q. The field orients says H⁰(B ∩ M₀) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' for the measurable M₀). Since singletons have H⁰-measure 1, B ∩ M₀ = ∅. So for x ∈ M₀ there are Q and an orthonormal τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with ζ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α or ζ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α; as Fin 0 is empty, τ is the empty tuple ⟨⟩. Hence ζ(x)(α) = s(x)·α(⟨⟩) with s(x) ∈ {1, −1}.
6. Formula. For a test 0-form g, S(g) = R.action(g) = ∫_{M₀} θ(x)ζ(x)(g(x)) dH⁰(x). The integrand is integrable on the finite set M₀, each singleton having finite measure (integrableOn_singleton_iff, integrableOn_finset_iUnion), so ∫_{M₀} h dH⁰ = Σ_{x∈F} H⁰({x})·h(x) = Σ_{x∈F} h(x) (setIntegral_finset). With step 5, S(g) = Σ_{x∈F} s(x)θ(x)·g(x)⟨⟩. Put m(x) := s(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ. By step 3, F = M₀ ⊆ spt S. ∎
proof_key_steps: μHE[0] gives mass 1 to every point, so every carrier point has positive R.measure.
(VO) gives M_{ℝ^P∖spt S}(S) = 0, so by (MR) the carrier lies in spt S.
Local integrability of θ ≥ 1 on the compact spt S makes the carrier finite.
The a.e. orientation condition holds at every carrier point, so ζ(x) = ±⟨·⟩.
The integral over the finite carrier is the finite sum S(g) = Σ ±θ(x)g(x)⟨⟩.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 5 (V4(i)), with all details supplied; Simon Ch. 6, 4.5(2)–(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 1235–1245) for the slicing identity behind (SL). The parent's extra assumption that X and ∂X have locally finite mass is not needed, because the IMRep measures used below are finite on compact sets. Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; M_W(X) := X.massOn W.
Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of X and ∂X, and let f be L-Lipschitz. Then f is continuous and E_t := {f < t} is a Borel set for every t (measurableSet_lt).
1. Slices. Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P (open), k := d, T := X and μ, μ', ξ, ξ', f, L; its hypotheses are exactly the admissibility assumptions (finiteness on compact subsets, a.e. strong measurability, a.e. bounds, the two representation formulas) and the Lipschitz property. It yields currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{E_t} ξ'(η) dμ' for all test forms, such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t satisfies M_G(Z_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open G and every t.
2. Z_t has locally finite mass for a.e. t. Fix k, m ∈ ℕ and apply (MM) with the constant sequence μ_j := μ, G := B_k(0) (open ball), (a, b) := (−m, m), L, and Z_j(t) := M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) for all j. Its hypotheses hold: f is continuous; μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ μ(B̄_k(0)) < ∞ since closed balls are compact; and for t ∈ (−m, m), Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_h h⁻¹μ(B_k(0) ∩ {t−h<f<t}) by step 1. (MM) gives a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m) and ∫_{(−m,m)} g ≤ L·liminf_j μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m<f<m}). The sequences are constant, so liminf_j Z_j(t) = M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) and the bound is L·μ(B_k(0) ∩ {−m<f<m}) < ∞ (Filter.liminf_const). A measurable function with finite integral over (−m, m) is finite a.e. there (ae_lt_top for volume.restrict (−m, m), then ae_restrict_iff'). Hence for a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) ⇒ M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞. Intersecting these countably many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff over m, then over k) and taking m > |t|, we get a Lebesgue-null set N such that M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for all k ∈ ℕ and all t ∉ N. If W is open with compact closure, then W is bounded, W ⊆ B_k(0) for some k, and M_W(Z_t) ≤ M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for t ∉ N (massOn_mono). Fix t ∉ N for steps 3–8.
3. Integrals against IMRep measures. Let R = (M_R, θ, ζ) be an IMRep in ℝ^P of degree q and ν := R.measure = (H^q⌞M_R) with density θ. (i) For compact K, ν(K) = ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ K} θ dH^q < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, field locallyIntegrable_mult). (ii) ν ≪ H^q⌞M_R (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous); hence ζ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient, AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac) and, by (IMC)(d), |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for ν-a.e. x and all α (AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le). (iii) For every Borel E and every q-form ω, ∫_E ζ(ω) dν = ∫_{M_R ∩ E} θ·ζ(ω) dH^q: indeed ν⌞E = ((H^q⌞M_R)⌞E) with density θ (restrict_withDensity) = (H^q⌞(E ∩ M_R)) with density θ (Measure.restrict_restrict), and ∫ h d(λ with density θ) = ∫ θ·h dλ for the measurable ℝ≥0-valued density x ↦ θ(x) (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul with f := fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ≥0); no integrability is needed). With E = ℝ^P this gives ∫ ζ(ω) dν = R.action(ω).
4. A_t is integer multiplicity. Let R_X be an IMRep of X. (IMC)(b) with E := E_t (Borel) gives a current A' and an IMRep R' representing A' with carrier M_{R_X} ∩ E_t, multiplicity θ_X and orientation ζ_X. Apply (RU) with k := d + 1, U := ℝ^P, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ, ξ), (μ₂, ξ₂) := (R_X.measure, ζ_X), (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): the finiteness, measurability and bound hypotheses hold by admissibility of (μ, ξ), by step 3(i)(ii), and trivially for the zero measure; the identity ∫ξ(ω)dμ = ∫ζ_X(ω)dR_X.measure + ∫0 d0 holds because both sides equal X(ω) (admissibility; step 3(iii) with E = ℝ^P and R_X.Represents X). (RU) with B := E_t and then step 3(iii) with E := E_t give, for every ω, A_t(ω) = ∫_{E_t} ξ(ω) dμ = ∫_{E_t} ζ_X(ω) dR_X.measure = ∫_{M_{R_X} ∩ E_t} θ_X ζ_X(ω) dH^{d+1} = R'.action(ω). So R' represents A_t and A_t is integer multiplicity.
5. B_t is integer multiplicity: the same argument with an IMRep R_∂ of ∂X (degree d), the pair (μ', ξ') and (RU) with k := d shows that the IMRep obtained from R_∂ by (IMC)(b) with E := E_t represents B_t.
6. ∂A_t is integer multiplicity. Let W be open with compact closure. (i) M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(closure W) < ∞: for a W-admissible η (tsupport η ⊆ W, |η(x)| ≤ 1), η(x) = 0 for x ∉ closure W, so |ξ'(x)(η(x))| ≤ |η(x)| ≤ 1_{closure W}(x) for μ'-a.e. x, and ofReal(B_t(η)) ≤ ‖∫_{E_t} ξ'(η) dμ'‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{E_t} ‖ξ'(η)‖ₑ dμ' ≤ ∫⁻_{E_t} 1_{closure W} dμ' ≤ μ'(closure W) (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm, lintegral_mono_ae, lintegral_indicator_one); take the supremum over η. (ii) M_W(Z_t) < ∞ by step 2. (iii) ∂A_t(η) = 1·Z_t(η) + 1·B_t(η) for every η, so the sibling cbr_cc_current_algebra (b) gives M_W(∂A_t) ≤ M_W(Z_t) + M_W(B_t) < ∞. Now BR(d) with U := ℝ^P and R := A_t (integer multiplicity by step 4) shows that ∂A_t is integer multiplicity.
7. Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) (ℝ^P is open; steps 5 and 6).
8. Conclusion. Let t ∉ N and let A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) satisfy A(ω) = ∫_{E_t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{E_t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms. Then A and A_t, and B and B_t, agree on all test forms, so A = A_t and B = B_t (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and ∂A − B = Z_t is integer multiplicity by step 7. Since N is null, this holds for L¹-a.e. t; as (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') and f were arbitrary, X has the integer slice property. ∎
proof_key_steps: (SL) provides slice currents A_t, B_t of X and the liminf bound for M_G(∂A_t − B_t).
